q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Seema said to him, "I will decorate the hall tomorrow."

Seema told him that I would decorate the hall the next day.
Seema told him that she would decorate the hall the previous day.
Seema said him that she would decorate the hall the next day.

q: Choose the word most similar in meaning to the given word: ABSTAIN
exp: ABSTAIN (परहेज़ करना, दूर रहना) — its synonym is 'forbear' (other synonyms: refrain, desist). 'indulge' is its antonym.

q: Choose the word most similar in meaning to the given word: CONDEMN
exp: CONDEMN (निंदा करना, दोषी ठहराना) — its synonym is 'blame' (other synonyms: denounce, disapprove). 'approve' is its antonym.

q: Choose the word most similar in meaning to the given word: PUNISH
exp: PUNISH (दंड देना) — its synonym is 'discipline' (other synonyms: penalise, chastise). 'reward' is its antonym.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: ACRIMONY
exp: ACRIMONY (कटुता, तीखापन) — its antonym is 'goodwill' (other antonyms: kindness). 'bitterness' is its synonym, not its antonym.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: LAUDABLE
exp: LAUDABLE (प्रशंसनीय) — its antonym is 'reprehensible' (other antonyms: blameworthy, shameful). 'praiseworthy' is its synonym, not its antonym. Other options: gregarious (मिलनसार, झुंड में रहने वाला).

q: Choose the word most similar in meaning to the given word: ANCESTOR
exp: ANCESTOR (पूर्वज) — its synonym is 'forefather' (other synonyms: forebear, predecessor). 'descendant' is its antonym.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: ANSWER
exp: ANSWER (उत्तर, जवाब) — its antonym is 'query' (other antonyms: question, enquiry). 'reply' is its synonym, not its antonym. Other options: defeat (पराजय, हार).

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: UGLY
exp: UGLY (कुरूप, बदसूरत) — its antonym is 'beautiful' (other antonyms: attractive, handsome). 'unsightly' is its synonym, not its antonym.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who hoards wealth and spends as little as possible
exp: 'One who hoards wealth and spends as little as possible' is called 'miser' (Hindi: कंजूस). Other options: debutant (पदार्पणकर्ता); sycophant (चाटुकार); oculist (नेत्र-चिकित्सक).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: STABLE
opts: A building where horses are kept
A place where arms and ammunition are stored
A place where coins are made
A place where fruit trees are grown
exp: STABLE (Hindi: अस्तबल) means: A building where horses are kept. The other options are the meanings of arsenal, orchard, mint respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Numismatics – The study or collection of coins
exp: 'Ichthyology' means 'The study of fishes' (मत्स्यविज्ञान), not 'The study of birds' (that is 'ornithology'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AQUATIC
exp: AQUATIC (Hindi: जलीय) means: Living or growing in water. The other options are the meanings of rural, invisible, oral respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who travels to a holy place for religious reasons
exp: 'One who travels to a holy place for religious reasons' is called 'pilgrim' (Hindi: तीर्थयात्री). Other options: cashier (ख़ज़ांची, रोकड़िया); renegade (दलबदलू, स्वधर्मत्यागी); gourmet (स्वादिष्ट भोजन का पारखी).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MORTUARY
opts: A hole dug by a rabbit or a fox
A place where dead bodies are kept for a short time
A collection of wild animals kept for exhibition
A place where grain is stored
exp: MORTUARY (Hindi: शवगृह) means: A place where dead bodies are kept for a short time. The other options are the meanings of granary, burrow, menagerie respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: PAEDIATRICIAN
opts: A doctor who specialises in children's diseases
One who has two spouses at the same time
One who collects or studies coins
exp: PAEDIATRICIAN (Hindi: बाल-रोग विशेषज्ञ) means: A doctor who specialises in children's diseases. The other options are the meanings of lexicographer, bigamist, numismatist respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Gregarious – Living in flocks or groups; fond of company
Incurable – That can be read easily
exp: 'Incurable' means 'That cannot be cured' (असाध्य), not 'That can be read easily' (that is 'legible'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
exp: Credulous (अंधविश्वासी, सहज-विश्वासी) means 'Ready to believe anything'. Correct meanings of the others: insectivorous = Feeding on insects; herbivorous = Feeding on plants; nuptial = Relating to marriage.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Irrevocable – That cannot be revoked or changed
exp: 'Diurnal' means 'Active during the daytime' (दिनचर), not 'Relating to horses' (that is 'equine'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Credulous – A fault that can be forgiven
Venial – Too great to be expressed in words
exp: Arboreal (वृक्षवासी) means 'Living in trees'. Correct meanings of the others: credulous = Ready to believe anything; venial = A fault that can be forgiven; ineffable = Too great to be expressed in words.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of ancient remains and monuments
exp: 'The study of ancient remains and monuments' is called 'archaeology' (Hindi: पुरातत्त्व). Other options: pathology (रोगविज्ञान); anthropology (मानवशास्त्र); geology (भूविज्ञान).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A published false statement damaging to a person's reputation
exp: 'A published false statement damaging to a person's reputation' is called 'libel' (Hindi: अपलेख, मानहानि-लेख). Other options: bribery (रिश्वतख़ोरी); arson (आगज़नी); dialect (बोली).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things
exp: 'Speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things' is called 'blasphemy' (Hindi: ईशनिंदा). Other options: fortnight (पखवाड़ा); perjury (झूठी गवाही); bouquet (गुलदस्ता).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who brings goods into a country secretly and illegally
exp: 'One who brings goods into a country secretly and illegally' is called 'smuggler' (Hindi: तस्कर). Other options: emigrant (उत्प्रवासी); optimist (आशावादी); creditor (लेनदार, ऋणदाता).

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Omniscient; (B) Euphemism; (C) Fraternal; (D) Omnipresent
List-II: (1) Relating to a brother; (2) One who knows everything; (3) A mild expression used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one; (4) One who is present everywhere
exp: Correct matching: Omniscient = One who knows everything; Euphemism = A mild expression used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one; Fraternal = Relating to a brother; Omnipresent = One who is present everywhere. Hence A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The act of making a false copy of a document or signature
exp: 'The act of making a false copy of a document or signature' is called 'forgery' (Hindi: जालसाज़ी). Other options: glossary (शब्दावली); synopsis (सारांश); constellation (तारामंडल).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of plants
exp: 'The study of plants' is called 'botany' (Hindi: वनस्पतिशास्त्र). Other options: astrology (ज्योतिष); horticulture (बागवानी, उद्यान-विज्ञान); zoology (प्राणिशास्त्र).

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Renegade – One who pretends to be what he is not
Fanatic – One who is filled with excessive and single-minded zeal
Auditor – One who checks and verifies accounts
Cashier – One who receives and pays out money in a bank or shop
exp: 'Renegade' means 'One who deserts his party or religion' (दलबदलू, स्वधर्मत्यागी), not 'One who pretends to be what he is not' (that is 'hypocrite'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ASTRAL
opts: Allowing light to pass through partially
exp: ASTRAL (Hindi: तारकीय) means: Relating to the stars. The other options are the meanings of inaccessible, hereditary, translucent respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Pacifist – One who always looks on the bright side of things
Sadist – One who opposes war and violence of any kind
Optimist – One who takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others
Apostate – One who abandons his religious faith
exp: Apostate (धर्मत्यागी) means 'One who abandons his religious faith'. Correct meanings of the others: optimist = One who always looks on the bright side of things; sadist = One who takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others; pacifist = One who opposes war and violence of any kind.

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Panacea; (B) Calligraphy; (C) Encyclopaedia; (D) Nepotism
List-II: (1) A remedy for all diseases or problems; (2) A book giving information on all branches of knowledge; (3) The art of beautiful handwriting; (4) Favouritism shown to relatives in matters of employment
exp: Correct matching: Panacea = A remedy for all diseases or problems; Calligraphy = The art of beautiful handwriting; Encyclopaedia = A book giving information on all branches of knowledge; Nepotism = Favouritism shown to relatives in matters of employment. Hence A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A collection of poems or other writings by various authors
exp: 'A collection of poems or other writings by various authors' is called 'anthology' (Hindi: संकलन). Other options: plagiarism (साहित्यिक चोरी); jargon (शब्दजाल, तकनीकी भाषा); bribery (रिश्वतख़ोरी).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: TAUTOLOGY
opts: Formation of a word from a sound associated with what is named
Needless repetition of the same idea in different words
The quality of never making mistakes
Repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words
exp: TAUTOLOGY (Hindi: पुनरुक्ति) means: Needless repetition of the same idea in different words. The other options are the meanings of alliteration, onomatopoeia, infallibility respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Perjury – The offence of telling a lie in court after taking an oath
Blasphemy – Copying another's work and passing it off as one's own
Fortnight – Speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things
Plagiarism – A period of fourteen days
exp: Perjury (झूठी गवाही) means 'The offence of telling a lie in court after taking an oath'. Correct meanings of the others: blasphemy = Speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things; plagiarism = Copying another's work and passing it off as one's own; fortnight = A period of fourteen days.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A place where monks live
exp: 'A place where monks live' is called 'monastery' (Hindi: मठ). Other options: arsenal (शस्त्रागार); library (पुस्तकालय); orchard (फलोद्यान).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: LANDLORD
opts: One who lets land or a building to a tenant
A man who has never married
One who does not eat or use any animal products
One who buys and sells goods or shares for others on commission
exp: LANDLORD (Hindi: मकान-मालिक) means: One who lets land or a building to a tenant. The other options are the meanings of vegan, bachelor, broker respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CHOREOGRAPHER
opts: One who is filled with excessive and single-minded zeal
A young person with exceptional qualities or abilities
exp: CHOREOGRAPHER (Hindi: नृत्य-निर्देशक) means: One who arranges dance steps. The other options are the meanings of veterinarian, prodigy, fanatic respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Belonging to or living at the same time
exp: 'Belonging to or living at the same time' is called 'contemporary' (Hindi: समकालीन). Other options: oral (मौखिक); edible (खाने योग्य); maternal (मातृक, मातृ-संबंधी).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One to whom money is owed
exp: 'One to whom money is owed' is called 'creditor' (Hindi: लेनदार, ऋणदाता). Other options: recluse (एकांतवासी); charlatan (ढोंगी, नीम-हकीम); cannibal (नरभक्षी).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of animals
exp: 'The study of animals' is called 'zoology' (Hindi: प्राणिशास्त्र). Other options: botany (वनस्पतिशास्त्र); oncology (अर्बुद-विज्ञान (कैंसर विज्ञान)); horticulture (बागवानी, उद्यान-विज्ञान).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: PROPRIETOR
opts: One who receives benefit from a will or insurance
One who is opposed to another
A young person with exceptional qualities or abilities
exp: PROPRIETOR (Hindi: स्वामी, मालिक) means: The owner of a business. The other options are the meanings of prodigy, antagonist, beneficiary respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Anaesthetic – A substance that makes one insensitive to pain
Hyperbole – A remedy for all diseases or problems
Panacea – Conduct or speech inciting people to rebel against the state
exp: Anaesthetic (निश्चेतक) means 'A substance that makes one insensitive to pain'. Correct meanings of the others: panacea = A remedy for all diseases or problems; sedition = Conduct or speech inciting people to rebel against the state; hyperbole = Deliberate exaggeration for effect.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Happening once every two years
exp: 'Happening once every two years' is called 'biennial' (Hindi: द्विवार्षिक (हर दो वर्ष में)). Other options: canine (श्वान-संबंधी); palpable (स्पर्शनीय, स्पष्ट); inexplicable (अवर्णनीय, अकथनीय (जिसे समझाया न जा सके)).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Relating to the hundredth anniversary
exp: 'Relating to the hundredth anniversary' is called 'centennial' (Hindi: शताब्दी-संबंधी). Other options: astral (तारकीय); canine (श्वान-संबंधी); auditory (श्रवण-संबंधी).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MIRAGE
opts: An optical illusion of water in the desert
A form of a language spoken in a particular region
Bringing goods into or out of a country illegally
Speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things
exp: MIRAGE (Hindi: मृगतृष्णा, मरीचिका) means: An optical illusion of water in the desert. The other options are the meanings of dialect, smuggling, blasphemy respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who makes an excessive display of learning
exp: 'One who makes an excessive display of learning' is called 'pedant' (Hindi: पांडित्य-प्रदर्शक). Other options: teetotaller (मद्यत्यागी); bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी); pedagogue (शिक्षक).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who makes things out of iron
exp: 'One who makes things out of iron' is called 'blacksmith' (Hindi: लोहार). Other options: tyrant (अत्याचारी शासक); pilgrim (तीर्थयात्री); bilingual (द्विभाषी).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: REFERENDUM
opts: A period of a thousand years
A book or document written by hand
A public declaration of policy by a political party
A direct vote by the people on a single political question
exp: REFERENDUM (Hindi: जनमत-संग्रह) means: A direct vote by the people on a single political question. The other options are the meanings of millennium, manuscript, manifesto respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ARCHIVES
opts: A place where coins are made
A place where arms and ammunition are stored
A place where government or historical records are kept
A place from where stars and planets are observed
exp: ARCHIVES (Hindi: अभिलेखागार) means: A place where government or historical records are kept. The other options are the meanings of arsenal, mint, observatory respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Optician – One who flatters others to gain favour
Anaesthetist – A doctor who administers anaesthetics
Bibliophile – One who makes or sells spectacles
exp: Anaesthetist (निश्चेतक-विशेषज्ञ) means 'A doctor who administers anaesthetics'. Correct meanings of the others: optician = One who makes or sells spectacles; sycophant = One who flatters others to gain favour; bibliophile = One who loves books.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Kleptomania – An irresistible urge to steal
Acrophobia – Fear of open or public places
exp: 'Acrophobia' means 'Fear of heights' (ऊँचाई का भय), not 'Fear of open or public places' (that is 'agoraphobia'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Government by those who steal from the nation's wealth
exp: 'Government by those who steal from the nation's wealth' is called 'kleptocracy' (Hindi: चोरतंत्र). Other options: matriarchy (मातृसत्ता); autocracy (निरंकुश शासन, एकतंत्र); patriarchy (पितृसत्ता).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: SEPTUAGENARIAN
opts: One who derives pleasure from his own pain
One who is between seventy and seventy-nine years old
One who is a hundred years old or more
exp: SEPTUAGENARIAN (Hindi: सत्तर वर्षीय) means: One who is between seventy and seventy-nine years old. The other options are the meanings of masochist, anaesthetist, centenarian respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: OCULAR
opts: Relating to the sense of smell
exp: OCULAR (Hindi: नेत्र-संबंधी) means: Relating to the eyes. The other options are the meanings of olfactory, incurable, culpable respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MONARCHY
opts: Government of the people, by the people, for the people
Government by a king or queen
Absence of government and law in a country
exp: MONARCHY (Hindi: राजतंत्र) means: Government by a king or queen. The other options are the meanings of democracy, anarchy, aristocracy respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A period of a hundred years
exp: 'A period of a hundred years' is called 'century' (Hindi: शताब्दी). Other options: cavalry (घुड़सवार सेना); crew (कर्मीदल); ordinance (अध्यादेश).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: TACTILE
opts: Relating to the sense of touch
That cannot be crossed or travelled over
exp: TACTILE (Hindi: स्पर्श-संबंधी) means: Relating to the sense of touch. The other options are the meanings of diurnal, carnivorous, impassable respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CARNIVOROUS
exp: CARNIVOROUS (Hindi: मांसाहारी) means: Feeding on flesh. The other options are the meanings of fastidious, culpable, incurable respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The killing of one's own father
exp: 'The killing of one's own father' is called 'patricide' (Hindi: पितृहत्या). Other options: germicide (रोगाणुनाशक); kleptocracy (चोरतंत्र); aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: HYPOCHONDRIA
opts: Fear of closed or narrow spaces
exp: HYPOCHONDRIA (Hindi: स्वास्थ्य-चिंता का रोग) means: Excessive anxiety about one's health. The other options are the meanings of claustrophobia, hydrophobia, cynophobia respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Elegy – A poem of mourning for the dead
Diction – The choice and use of words in speech or writing
Euphemism – A mild expression used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one
exp: 'Alimony' means 'An allowance paid to a wife or husband after divorce' (गुज़ारा-भत्ता), not 'The lowest point' (that is 'nadir'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A teacher, especially a strict one
exp: 'A teacher, especially a strict one' is called 'pedagogue' (Hindi: शिक्षक). Other options: lexicographer (कोशकार); sceptic (संशयवादी); sycophant (चाटुकार).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Relating to the teeth
exp: 'Relating to the teeth' is called 'dental' (Hindi: दाँत-संबंधी). Other options: contemporary (समकालीन); edible (खाने योग्य); solar (सौर).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AUDIENCE
opts: A list of books referred to in a scholarly work
An imitation of a writer's style for comic effect
A group of people who listen to a speech or performance
exp: AUDIENCE (Hindi: श्रोतागण) means: A group of people who listen to a speech or performance. The other options are the meanings of fleet, parody, bibliography respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CARTOGRAPHY
opts: The art of writing or solving codes
The study of the origin of words
exp: CARTOGRAPHY (Hindi: मानचित्र-कला) means: The art of making maps. The other options are the meanings of cryptography, etymology, calligraphy respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Posthumous – In exactly the same words
Irreconcilable – Occurring or published after a person's death
exp: Inimitable (अनुपम, अनुकरण न करने योग्य) means 'That cannot be imitated'. Correct meanings of the others: posthumous = Occurring or published after a person's death; verbatim = In exactly the same words; irreconcilable = That cannot be reconciled.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Mausoleum – A large and magnificent tomb
Sanatorium – A place where grain is stored
Granary – A place where dead bodies are kept for a short time
Mortuary – A place for the treatment of invalids or convalescents
exp: Mausoleum (मक़बरा, भव्य समाधि) means 'A large and magnificent tomb'. Correct meanings of the others: sanatorium = A place for the treatment of invalids or convalescents; granary = A place where grain is stored; mortuary = A place where dead bodies are kept for a short time.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: PATERNAL
opts: Relating to the sense of hearing
Relating to the life of shepherds or the countryside
exp: PATERNAL (Hindi: पैतृक, पितृ-संबंधी) means: Relating to a father. The other options are the meanings of renal, auditory, pastoral respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: HONORARY
opts: Fit to be chosen or qualified for something
Holding a position without being paid for it
exp: HONORARY (Hindi: अवैतनिक, मानद) means: Holding a position without being paid for it. The other options are the meanings of marine, eligible, obsolete respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: DIURNAL
opts: That cannot be revoked or changed
exp: DIURNAL (Hindi: दिनचर) means: Active during the daytime. The other options are the meanings of irrevocable, equine, culpable respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: DEN
opts: The lair of a wild animal such as a lion
A place where government or historical records are kept
A place where coins are made
A place from where stars and planets are observed
exp: DEN (Hindi: माँद) means: The lair of a wild animal such as a lion. The other options are the meanings of observatory, archives, mint respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who never takes alcoholic drinks
exp: 'One who never takes alcoholic drinks' is called 'teetotaller' (Hindi: मद्यत्यागी). Other options: theist (आस्तिक); paediatrician (बाल-रोग विशेषज्ञ); optician (चश्मासाज़).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A group of cattle
exp: 'A group of cattle' is called 'herd' (Hindi: पशुओं का झुंड). Other options: referendum (जनमत-संग्रह); flock (झुंड (भेड़/पक्षी)); amnesty (आम माफ़ी, क्षमादान).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Easily broken
exp: 'Easily broken' is called 'fragile' (Hindi: भंगुर, नाज़ुक). Other options: aquatic (जलीय); transparent (पारदर्शी); annual (वार्षिक).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A mild expression used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one
exp: 'A mild expression used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one' is called 'euphemism' (Hindi: प्रियोक्ति, मृदूक्ति). Other options: eulogy (प्रशस्ति, स्तुति-भाषण); equinox (विषुव); elegy (शोकगीत).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who is between eighty and eighty-nine years old

An irresistible urge to set things on fire
A deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin
exp: ACROPHOBIA (Hindi: ऊँचाई का भय) means: Fear of heights. The other options are the meanings of pyromania, anaemia, megalomania respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who designs buildings
exp: 'One who designs buildings' is called 'architect' (Hindi: वास्तुकार). Other options: tailor (दर्ज़ी); veteran (अनुभवी, पुराना योद्धा); hostage (बंधक).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CENTURY
opts: A direct vote by the people on a single political question
A group of people assembled for religious worship
A period of a hundred years
exp: CENTURY (Hindi: शताब्दी) means: A period of a hundred years. The other options are the meanings of herd, congregation, referendum respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A system or period of government
exp: 'A system or period of government' is called 'regime' (Hindi: शासनकाल, शासन-प्रणाली). Other options: millennium (सहस्राब्दी); vaccine (टीका); sabotage (तोड़फोड़).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: An optical illusion of water in the desert
exp: 'An optical illusion of water in the desert' is called 'mirage' (Hindi: मृगतृष्णा, मरीचिका). Other options: placebo (प्लेसीबो (भ्रामक औषधि)); monologue (एकालाप); bouquet (गुलदस्ता).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MUTINY
opts: An open rebellion against authority, especially by soldiers or sailors
A long speech by one person
An optical illusion of water in the desert
A written statement confirmed by oath for use as evidence in court
exp: MUTINY (Hindi: सैनिक विद्रोह, ग़दर) means: An open rebellion against authority, especially by soldiers or sailors. The other options are the meanings of affidavit, mirage, monologue respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: GREGARIOUS
opts: Living in flocks or groups; fond of company
exp: GREGARIOUS (Hindi: झुंड में रहने वाला, मिलनसार) means: Living in flocks or groups; fond of company. The other options are the meanings of fortuitous, fastidious, fraternal respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: SATIRE
opts: The life story of a person written by himself
A public declaration of policy by a political party
A period of a thousand years
The use of humour or ridicule to expose people's folly
exp: SATIRE (Hindi: व्यंग्य) means: The use of humour or ridicule to expose people's folly. The other options are the meanings of millennium, autobiography, manifesto respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MONOTHEISM
opts: Formation of a word from a sound associated with what is named
A common language used between speakers of different languages
Repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words
exp: MONOTHEISM (Hindi: एकेश्वरवाद) means: Belief in only one God. The other options are the meanings of lingua franca, onomatopoeia, alliteration respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: That cannot be avoided
exp: 'That cannot be avoided' is called 'inevitable' (Hindi: अपरिहार्य, अवश्यंभावी). Other options: contemporary (समकालीन); unanimous (सर्वसम्मत); rural (ग्रामीण).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Relating to the stars
exp: 'Relating to the stars' is called 'astral' (Hindi: तारकीय). Other options: intolerable (असहनीय); inexplicable (अवर्णनीय, अकथनीय (जिसे समझाया न जा सके)); paternal (पैतृक, पितृ-संबंधी).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A place where fish are kept
exp: 'A place where fish are kept' is called 'aquarium' (Hindi: मछलीघर). Other options: hive (मधुमक्खी का छत्ता); hangar (विमानशाला); orphanage (अनाथालय).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A building where horses are kept
exp: 'A building where horses are kept' is called 'stable' (Hindi: अस्तबल). Other options: observatory (वेधशाला); monastery (मठ); cemetery (क़ब्रिस्तान).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: FORGERY
opts: The act of making a false copy of a document or signature
An idea or phrase that has been overused
A false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation
exp: FORGERY (Hindi: जालसाज़ी) means: The act of making a false copy of a document or signature. The other options are the meanings of constellation, slander, cliché respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: LINGUA FRANCA
opts: A word that reads the same backwards as forwards
A common language used between speakers of different languages
The quality of using more words than needed
Speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, especially in a play
exp: LINGUA FRANCA (Hindi: संपर्क भाषा) means: A common language used between speakers of different languages. The other options are the meanings of soliloquy, verbosity, palindrome respectively.

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Masochist; (B) Anaesthetist; (C) Lexicography; (D) Insectivorous
List-II: (1) Feeding on insects; (2) The art of compiling dictionaries; (3) A doctor who administers anaesthetics; (4) One who derives pleasure from his own pain
exp: Correct matching: Masochist = One who derives pleasure from his own pain; Anaesthetist = A doctor who administers anaesthetics; Lexicography = The art of compiling dictionaries; Insectivorous = Feeding on insects. Hence A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin
exp: 'A deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin' is called 'anaemia' (Hindi: रक्ताल्पता). Other options: claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय); hydrophobia (जलभीति); cynophobia (कुत्तों का भय).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: VERBATIM
opts: Occurring or published after a person's death
That cannot be erased or removed
exp: VERBATIM (Hindi: शब्दशः) means: In exactly the same words. The other options are the meanings of indelible, posthumous, hepatic respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who eats too much
exp: 'One who eats too much' is called 'glutton' (Hindi: पेटू). Other options: nonagenarian (नब्बे वर्षीय); iconoclast (मूर्तिभंजक); polyglot (बहुभाषी).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A cruel and oppressive ruler
exp: 'A cruel and oppressive ruler' is called 'tyrant' (Hindi: अत्याचारी शासक). Other options: antagonist (विरोधी, प्रतिनायक); mediator (मध्यस्थ); veterinarian (पशु-चिकित्सक).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Fear of darkness
exp: 'Fear of darkness' is called 'nyctophobia' (Hindi: अंधकार का भय). Other options: monophobia (अकेलेपन का भय); claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय); hypochondria (स्वास्थ्य-चिंता का रोग).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A doctor who specialises in children's diseases
exp: 'A doctor who specialises in children's diseases' is called 'paediatrician' (Hindi: बाल-रोग विशेषज्ञ). Other options: sexagenarian (साठ वर्षीय); gynaecologist (स्त्री-रोग विशेषज्ञ); egoist (स्वार्थी, अहंवादी).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The point in the sky directly overhead
exp: 'The point in the sky directly overhead' is called 'zenith' (Hindi: शिरोबिंदु, चरम बिंदु). Other options: glossary (शब्दावली); affidavit (शपथ-पत्र, हलफ़नामा); endemic (स्थानिक रोग).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: NOSTALGIA
opts: A sentimental longing for the past
exp: NOSTALGIA (Hindi: अतीत की याद) means: A sentimental longing for the past. The other options are the meanings of insomnia, amnesia, xenophobia respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: REGICIDE
opts: A substance used for killing germs
exp: REGICIDE (Hindi: राजहत्या) means: The killing of a king. The other options are the meanings of germicide, aristocracy, plutocracy respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ARCHITECT
opts: One who lets land or a building to a tenant
One who has been forced to leave his country to escape war or persecution
A man who has never married
exp: ARCHITECT (Hindi: वास्तुकार) means: One who designs buildings. The other options are the meanings of refugee, landlord, bachelor respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: BIGAMIST
opts: One who hoards wealth and spends as little as possible
One who has two spouses at the same time
exp: BIGAMIST (Hindi: द्विविवाही) means: One who has two spouses at the same time. The other options are the meanings of miser, cartographer, misanthrope respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: FEASIBLE
opts: Belonging to or living at the same time
exp: FEASIBLE (Hindi: व्यवहार्य, संभव) means: That can be done easily. The other options are the meanings of inevitable, contemporary, portable respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Active during the daytime
exp: 'Active during the daytime' is called 'diurnal' (Hindi: दिनचर). Other options: incurable (असाध्य); equine (अश्व-संबंधी); insolvent (दिवालिया).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The use of humour or ridicule to expose people's folly
exp: 'The use of humour or ridicule to expose people's folly' is called 'satire' (Hindi: व्यंग्य). Other options: fleet (बेड़ा); coup (तख़्तापलट); autobiography (आत्मकथा).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MORATORIUM
opts: A remedy for all diseases or problems
An allowance paid to a wife or husband after divorce
A word formed by rearranging the letters of another word
A temporary suspension of an activity or payment
exp: MORATORIUM (Hindi: स्थगन, अधिस्थगन) means: A temporary suspension of an activity or payment. The other options are the meanings of alimony, anagram, panacea respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Centennial – Allowing light to pass through partially
Opaque – That cannot be seen through
Biennial – Happening once every two years
exp: 'Centennial' means 'Relating to the hundredth anniversary' (शताब्दी-संबंधी), not 'Allowing light to pass through partially' (that is 'translucent'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: GERONTOCRACY
opts: Government by one person with absolute power
A social system ruled or headed by men
A social system ruled or headed by women
exp: GERONTOCRACY (Hindi: वृद्धतंत्र) means: Government by old people. The other options are the meanings of matriarchy, autocracy, patriarchy respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: VERSATILE
opts: A disease that spreads by contact
Able to do many different things well
exp: VERSATILE (Hindi: बहुमुखी प्रतिभा वाला) means: Able to do many different things well. The other options are the meanings of mortal, contagious, spontaneous respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Ascetic – One who believes that nothing can be known about the existence of God
Emigrant – One who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from all pleasures
Agnostic – One who leaves his own country to settle in another
Pacifist – One who opposes war and violence of any kind
exp: Pacifist (शांतिवादी) means 'One who opposes war and violence of any kind'. Correct meanings of the others: agnostic = One who believes that nothing can be known about the existence of God; emigrant = One who leaves his own country to settle in another; ascetic = One who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from all pleasures.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CELIBATE
opts: One who is excessively in love with himself
One who abstains from marriage and sexual relations
One who always looks on the bright side of things
One who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive
exp: CELIBATE (Hindi: ब्रह्मचारी) means: One who abstains from marriage and sexual relations. The other options are the meanings of impostor, optimist, narcissist respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who believes in the existence of God
exp: 'One who believes in the existence of God' is called 'theist' (Hindi: आस्तिक). Other options: bigamist (द्विविवाही); calligrapher (सुलेखक); busybody (दूसरों के काम में दख़ल देने वाला).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: BURGLARY
opts: A false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation
Breaking into a house to steal
Medical examination of a dead body to find the cause of death
A short story with animals as characters that teaches a moral
exp: BURGLARY (Hindi: सेंधमारी) means: Breaking into a house to steal. The other options are the meanings of fable, slander, post-mortem respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Lexicographer – One who compiles a dictionary
Centenarian – One who is a hundred years old or more
Polyglot – One who attacks cherished beliefs or breaks religious images
exp: 'Polyglot' means 'One who can speak many languages' (बहुभाषी), not 'One who attacks cherished beliefs or breaks religious images' (that is 'iconoclast'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ESPIONAGE
opts: A thing kept as a reminder of a person, place or event
A concluding section at the end of a book or play
Medical examination of a dead body to find the cause of death
exp: ESPIONAGE (Hindi: जासूसी) means: The practice of spying. The other options are the meanings of souvenir, epilogue, post-mortem respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: INSECTICIDE
opts: A substance used for killing insects
Government of the people, by the people, for the people
Government by priests or religious leaders
exp: INSECTICIDE (Hindi: कीटनाशक) means: A substance used for killing insects. The other options are the meanings of infanticide, theocracy, democracy respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A list of books referred to in a scholarly work
exp: 'A list of books referred to in a scholarly work' is called 'bibliography' (Hindi: ग्रंथसूची). Other options: ordinance (अध्यादेश); crew (कर्मीदल); vaccine (टीका).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AUTOCRAT
opts: One who is between sixty and sixty-nine years old
A ruler who has absolute power
One who meddles in other people's affairs
exp: AUTOCRAT (Hindi: निरंकुश शासक) means: A ruler who has absolute power. The other options are the meanings of cartographer, sexagenarian, busybody respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AMPHIBIAN
opts: Favouritism shown to relatives in matters of employment
An animal that can live both on land and in water
An allowance paid to a wife or husband after divorce
A story in which characters and events stand for abstract ideas
exp: AMPHIBIAN (Hindi: उभयचर) means: An animal that can live both on land and in water. The other options are the meanings of nepotism, alimony, allegory respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Needless repetition of the same idea in different words
exp: 'Needless repetition of the same idea in different words' is called 'tautology' (Hindi: पुनरुक्ति). Other options: alliteration (अनुप्रास); pantheism (सर्वेश्वरवाद); onomatopoeia (ध्वन्यात्मक शब्द-रचना).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Relating to a town or city
exp: 'Relating to a town or city' is called 'urban' (Hindi: शहरी). Other options: manual (हस्तचालित, हाथ का); solar (सौर); fragile (भंगुर, नाज़ुक).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: TANGIBLE
opts: Belonging to or living at the same time
That is real and can be perceived by touch
Holding a position without being paid for it
exp: TANGIBLE (Hindi: मूर्त, ठोस) means: That is real and can be perceived by touch. The other options are the meanings of contemporary, honorary, inevitable respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: QUARANTINE
opts: The life story of a person written by himself
A public declaration of policy by a political party
Isolation of a person to prevent the spread of infection
exp: QUARANTINE (Hindi: संगरोध, एकांतवास) means: Isolation of a person to prevent the spread of infection. The other options are the meanings of manifesto, autopsy, autobiography respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CREDITOR
opts: A doctor who specialises in heart diseases
One who lives alone and avoids other people
One to whom money is owed
One who opposes war and violence of any kind
exp: CREDITOR (Hindi: लेनदार, ऋणदाता) means: One to whom money is owed. The other options are the meanings of cardiologist, recluse, pacifist respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The fiftieth anniversary
exp: 'The fiftieth anniversary' is called 'golden jubilee' (Hindi: स्वर्ण जयंती). Other options: affidavit (शपथ-पत्र, हलफ़नामा); endemic (स्थानिक रोग); burglary (सेंधमारी).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AMATEUR
opts: One who lets land or a building to a tenant
One who pays rent for the use of land or a building
A young person below the age of adulthood
One who does something as a hobby and not as a profession
exp: AMATEUR (Hindi: शौक़िया) means: One who does something as a hobby and not as a profession. The other options are the meanings of landlord, tenant, juvenile respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AMBIGUOUS
opts: Having more than one possible meaning
exp: AMBIGUOUS (Hindi: द्विअर्थी, अस्पष्ट) means: Having more than one possible meaning. The other options are the meanings of portable, edible, manual respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: OASIS
opts: A fertile spot in a desert where water is found
A place where aircraft are kept
exp: OASIS (Hindi: मरूद्यान, नख़लिस्तान) means: A fertile spot in a desert where water is found. The other options are the meanings of hive, hangar, kennel respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A general pardon granted by a government to offenders
exp: 'A general pardon granted by a government to offenders' is called 'amnesty' (Hindi: आम माफ़ी, क्षमादान). Other options: millennium (सहस्राब्दी); autopsy (शव-परीक्षण); referendum (जनमत-संग्रह).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A fee paid for professional services nominally rendered without charge
exp: 'A fee paid for professional services nominally rendered without charge' is called 'honorarium' (Hindi: मानदेय). Other options: alliteration (अनुप्रास); palindrome (विलोमपद (उलटा-सीधा समान शब्द)); verbosity (शब्दाडंबर).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CARDIOLOGIST
opts: A doctor who treats skin diseases
A doctor who specialises in heart diseases
One who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from all pleasures
exp: CARDIOLOGIST (Hindi: हृदय-रोग विशेषज्ञ) means: A doctor who specialises in heart diseases. The other options are the meanings of dermatologist, debtor, ascetic respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Irreparable – That cannot be crossed or travelled over
Sylvan – Relating to woods or forests
exp: Sylvan (वन-संबंधी) means 'Relating to woods or forests'. Correct meanings of the others: irreparable = That cannot be repaired; impassable = That cannot be crossed or travelled over; omnipotent = One who is all-powerful.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Fear of open or public places
exp: 'Fear of open or public places' is called 'agoraphobia' (Hindi: खुले स्थान का भय). Other options: acrophobia (ऊँचाई का भय); ailurophobia (बिल्लियों का भय); hypochondria (स्वास्थ्य-चिंता का रोग).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ZOOLOGY
opts: The study of family history and lineage
The study of tumours and cancer
The art of growing fruits, flowers and vegetables
exp: ZOOLOGY (Hindi: प्राणिशास्त्र) means: The study of animals. The other options are the meanings of horticulture, oncology, genealogy respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who buys and sells goods or shares for others on commission
exp: 'One who buys and sells goods or shares for others on commission' is called 'broker' (Hindi: दलाल). Other options: vegan (पूर्ण शाकाहारी (वीगन)); dentist (दंत-चिकित्सक); patriot (देशभक्त).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AUDITORY
opts: Relating to the sense of hearing
exp: AUDITORY (Hindi: श्रवण-संबंधी) means: Relating to the sense of hearing. The other options are the meanings of centennial, intolerable, audible respectively.

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Diction; (B) Omnipresent; (C) Amphibian; (D) Sadist
List-II: (1) One who takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others; (2) The choice and use of words in speech or writing; (3) One who is present everywhere; (4) An animal that can live both on land and in water
exp: Correct matching: Diction = The choice and use of words in speech or writing; Omnipresent = One who is present everywhere; Amphibian = An animal that can live both on land and in water; Sadist = One who takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others. Hence A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: KLEPTOCRACY
opts: Government by those who steal from the nation's wealth
A social system ruled or headed by men
Government by one person with absolute power
A social system ruled or headed by women
exp: KLEPTOCRACY (Hindi: चोरतंत्र) means: Government by those who steal from the nation's wealth. The other options are the meanings of matriarchy, patriarchy, autocracy respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MORTAL
exp: MORTAL (Hindi: नश्वर) means: Subject to death. The other options are the meanings of inevitable, fragile, solar respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: THANATOPHOBIA
opts: Fear of closed or narrow spaces
exp: THANATOPHOBIA (Hindi: मृत्यु का भय) means: Fear of death. The other options are the meanings of claustrophobia, hydrophobia, nyctophobia respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who owes money
exp: 'One who owes money' is called 'debtor' (Hindi: देनदार, ऋणी). Other options: spinster (अविवाहित स्त्री); nomad (ख़ानाबदोश, घुमंतू); usurper (अनधिकार सत्ता-हरणकर्ता).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of the heart
exp: 'The study of the heart' is called 'cardiology' (Hindi: हृदयरोग-विज्ञान). Other options: cryptography (गूढ़लेखन); etymology (शब्द-व्युत्पत्ति विज्ञान); calligraphy (सुलेख).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: An introductory section of a play or book
exp: 'An introductory section of a play or book' is called 'prologue' (Hindi: प्रस्तावना). Other options: diamond jubilee (हीरक जयंती); antidote (विषनाशक दवा); slander (मौखिक मानहानि).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who makes things out of wood
exp: 'One who makes things out of wood' is called 'carpenter' (Hindi: बढ़ई). Other options: architect (वास्तुकार); bachelor (अविवाहित पुरुष); heir (उत्तराधिकारी).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ICONOCLAST
opts: One who attacks cherished beliefs or breaks religious images
One who is between sixty and sixty-nine years old
One who believes in the existence of God
One who has only one spouse at a time
exp: ICONOCLAST (Hindi: मूर्तिभंजक) means: One who attacks cherished beliefs or breaks religious images. The other options are the meanings of monogamist, theist, sexagenarian respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: SYCOPHANT
opts: One who is a hundred years old or more
One who flatters others to gain favour
exp: SYCOPHANT (Hindi: चाटुकार) means: One who flatters others to gain favour. The other options are the meanings of centenarian, misanthrope, spendthrift respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A place where weapons are kept
exp: 'A place where weapons are kept' is called 'armoury' (Hindi: शस्त्रागार (हथियार-घर)). Other options: mortuary (शवगृह); dormitory (शयनागार); mausoleum (मक़बरा, भव्य समाधि).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of religion and God

exp: OCTOGENARIAN (Hindi: अस्सी वर्षीय) means: One who is between eighty and eighty-nine years old. The other options are the meanings of polygamist, lexicographer, theist respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Relating to tailoring or clothes
exp: 'Relating to tailoring or clothes' is called 'sartorial' (Hindi: वस्त्र-संबंधी). Other options: illegible (अपठनीय); herbivorous (शाकाहारी (जीव)); venial (क्षम्य).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Fear of heights
exp: 'Fear of heights' is called 'acrophobia' (Hindi: ऊँचाई का भय). Other options: pyrophobia (अग्नि-भय); ailurophobia (बिल्लियों का भय); hypochondria (स्वास्थ्य-चिंता का रोग).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Soldiers who fight on horseback
exp: 'Soldiers who fight on horseback' is called 'cavalry' (Hindi: घुड़सवार सेना). Other options: quarantine (संगरोध, एकांतवास); decade (दशक); regime (शासनकाल, शासन-प्रणाली).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: EULOGY
opts: A temporary suspension of an activity or payment
A substance that makes one insensitive to pain
The time when the sun reaches its highest or lowest point at noon
A speech or writing in praise of a person, especially one who has died
exp: EULOGY (Hindi: प्रशस्ति, स्तुति-भाषण) means: A speech or writing in praise of a person, especially one who has died. The other options are the meanings of solstice, moratorium, anaesthetic respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MENAGERIE
opts: A place for the treatment of invalids or convalescents
A place where dead bodies are burnt
A place where weapons are kept
A collection of wild animals kept for exhibition
exp: MENAGERIE (Hindi: चिड़ियाघर, पशुशाला) means: A collection of wild animals kept for exhibition. The other options are the meanings of crematorium, sanatorium, armoury respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Leonine – Relating to the sense of taste
exp: Illegible (अपठनीय) means 'That cannot be read'. Correct meanings of the others: leonine = Relating to lions; gustatory = Relating to the sense of taste; credulous = Ready to believe anything.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who lives alone and avoids other people
exp: 'One who lives alone and avoids other people' is called 'recluse' (Hindi: एकांतवासी). Other options: pessimist (निराशावादी); impostor (छद्मवेशी, धोखेबाज़); emigrant (उत्प्रवासी).

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Monarchy – Government by a king or queen
Bureaucracy – A social system ruled or headed by men
Democracy – Government of the people, by the people, for the people
Anarchy – Absence of government and law in a country
exp: 'Bureaucracy' means 'Government by officials' (नौकरशाही), not 'A social system ruled or headed by men' (that is 'patriarchy'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of insects
exp: 'The study of insects' is called 'entomology' (Hindi: कीटविज्ञान). Other options: dermatology (त्वचा-विज्ञान); cryptography (गूढ़लेखन); cartography (मानचित्र-कला).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: RENEGADE
opts: One who has escaped from captivity or is running away from justice
One who lives a solitary life for religious reasons
One who deserts his party or religion
exp: RENEGADE (Hindi: दलबदलू, स्वधर्मत्यागी) means: One who deserts his party or religion. The other options are the meanings of hermit, fugitive, proprietor respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: SUICIDE
opts: A substance used for destroying pests
Government of the people, by the people, for the people
exp: SUICIDE (Hindi: आत्महत्या) means: The act of killing oneself. The other options are the meanings of pesticide, bureaucracy, democracy respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Megalomania – A mania for power or grandeur
Hypochondria – Excessive anxiety about one's health
Kleptomania – Fear of open or public places
exp: 'Kleptomania' means 'An irresistible urge to steal' (चोरी करने की सनक), not 'Fear of open or public places' (that is 'agoraphobia'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who attacks cherished beliefs or breaks religious images
exp: 'One who attacks cherished beliefs or breaks religious images' is called 'iconoclast' (Hindi: मूर्तिभंजक). Other options: cartographer (मानचित्रकार); spendthrift (फ़िज़ूलख़र्च); eavesdropper (छिपकर बातें सुनने वाला).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ELIGIBLE
opts: Fit to be chosen or qualified for something
exp: ELIGIBLE (Hindi: पात्र, योग्य) means: Fit to be chosen or qualified for something. The other options are the meanings of anonymous, manual, cardiac respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Sadist – A man whose wife is dead
Widower – One who leaves his own country to settle in another
Pessimist – One who always looks on the dark side of things
Emigrant – One who takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others
exp: Pessimist (निराशावादी) means 'One who always looks on the dark side of things'. Correct meanings of the others: widower = A man whose wife is dead; emigrant = One who leaves his own country to settle in another; sadist = One who takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A pen where pigs are kept
exp: 'A pen where pigs are kept' is called 'sty' (Hindi: सुअरबाड़ा). Other options: abattoir (कसाईख़ाना, बूचड़खाना); apiary (मधुमक्खी-शाला); eyrie (चील या बाज़ का घोंसला).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Fear of death
exp: 'Fear of death' is called 'thanatophobia' (Hindi: मृत्यु का भय). Other options: claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय); anaemia (रक्ताल्पता); megalomania (महत्ता-सनक, सत्ता का उन्माद).

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Itinerary; (B) Tyrant; (C) Bureaucracy; (D) Silver jubilee
List-II: (1) Government by officials; (2) A cruel and oppressive ruler; (3) A planned route or plan of a journey; (4) The twenty-fifth anniversary
exp: Correct matching: Itinerary = A planned route or plan of a journey; Tyrant = A cruel and oppressive ruler; Bureaucracy = Government by officials; Silver jubilee = The twenty-fifth anniversary. Hence A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4.

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Mercenary; (B) Libel; (C) Renal; (D) Zenith
List-II: (1) A published false statement damaging to a person's reputation; (2) Relating to the kidneys; (3) A soldier who fights for any country for money; (4) The point in the sky directly overhead
exp: Correct matching: Mercenary = A soldier who fights for any country for money; Libel = A published false statement damaging to a person's reputation; Renal = Relating to the kidneys; Zenith = The point in the sky directly overhead. Hence A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive
exp: 'One who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive' is called 'impostor' (Hindi: छद्मवेशी, धोखेबाज़). Other options: cardiologist (हृदय-रोग विशेषज्ञ); smuggler (तस्कर); misogynist (स्त्री-द्वेषी).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of tumours and cancer
exp: 'The study of tumours and cancer' is called 'oncology' (Hindi: अर्बुद-विज्ञान (कैंसर विज्ञान)). Other options: botany (वनस्पतिशास्त्र); horticulture (बागवानी, उद्यान-विज्ञान); genealogy (वंशावली-विज्ञान).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: VETERINARIAN
opts: One who watches a show or game
One who brings a case against another in a court of law
One who intervenes between two parties to bring about an agreement
exp: VETERINARIAN (Hindi: पशु-चिकित्सक) means: A doctor who treats animals. The other options are the meanings of plaintiff, spectator, mediator respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: SCULPTOR
opts: One who pretends to be what he is not
One who is indifferent to pleasure and pain
One who carves figures in stone or wood
One who can speak two languages fluently
exp: SCULPTOR (Hindi: मूर्तिकार) means: One who carves figures in stone or wood. The other options are the meanings of hypocrite, stoic, bilingual respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who is all-powerful
exp: 'One who is all-powerful' is called 'omnipotent' (Hindi: सर्वशक्तिमान). Other options: indelible (अमिट); olfactory (घ्राण-संबंधी); posthumous (मरणोपरांत).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Belief in only one God
exp: 'Belief in only one God' is called 'monotheism' (Hindi: एकेश्वरवाद). Other options: palindrome (विलोमपद (उलटा-सीधा समान शब्द)); lingua franca (संपर्क भाषा); verbosity (शब्दाडंबर).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: TREASON
opts: Deliberate destruction of property to obstruct something
A substance used to produce immunity against a disease
The crime of betraying one's country
exp: TREASON (Hindi: राजद्रोह) means: The crime of betraying one's country. The other options are the meanings of decade, vaccine, sabotage respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: IMPASSABLE
opts: That cannot be crossed or travelled over
That cannot be captured or broken into
exp: IMPASSABLE (Hindi: अगम्य, दुर्गम) means: That cannot be crossed or travelled over. The other options are the meanings of sylvan, omniscient, impregnable respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Living or growing in water
exp: 'Living or growing in water' is called 'aquatic' (Hindi: जलीय). Other options: rural (ग्रामीण); oral (मौखिक); spontaneous (स्वतःस्फूर्त).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: HERD
opts: Deliberate destruction of property to obstruct something
The life story of a person written by someone else
A disease prevalent over a whole country or the world
exp: HERD (Hindi: पशुओं का झुंड) means: A group of cattle. The other options are the meanings of biography, sabotage, pandemic respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who has only one spouse at a time
exp: 'One who has only one spouse at a time' is called 'monogamist' (Hindi: एकविवाही). Other options: egoist (स्वार्थी, अहंवादी); bigamist (द्विविवाही); cartographer (मानचित्रकार).

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Honorarium – Needless repetition of the same idea in different words
Tautology – The belief that God is present in everything
Infallibility – The quality of never making mistakes
Pantheism – A fee paid for professional services nominally rendered without charge
exp: Infallibility (अचूकता) means 'The quality of never making mistakes'. Correct meanings of the others: honorarium = A fee paid for professional services nominally rendered without charge; tautology = Needless repetition of the same idea in different words; pantheism = The belief that God is present in everything.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who has long experience in a particular field
exp: 'One who has long experience in a particular field' is called 'veteran' (Hindi: अनुभवी, पुराना योद्धा). Other options: amateur (शौक़िया); vegetarian (शाकाहारी); dictator (तानाशाह).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: EUPHEMISM
opts: A mild expression used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one
The choice and use of words in speech or writing
A word formed by rearranging the letters of another word
Conduct or speech inciting people to rebel against the state
exp: EUPHEMISM (Hindi: प्रियोक्ति, मृदूक्ति) means: A mild expression used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one. The other options are the meanings of sedition, anagram, diction respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
exp: Renal (गुर्दा-संबंधी) means 'Relating to the kidneys'. Correct meanings of the others: astral = Relating to the stars; incomprehensible = That cannot be understood; avian = Relating to birds.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Septuagenarian – One who derives pleasure from his own pain
Octogenarian – One who is between seventy and seventy-nine years old
Debutant – One who makes a first appearance in public or in a sport
Masochist – One who is between eighty and eighty-nine years old
exp: Debutant (पदार्पणकर्ता) means 'One who makes a first appearance in public or in a sport'. Correct meanings of the others: masochist = One who derives pleasure from his own pain; octogenarian = One who is between eighty and eighty-nine years old; septuagenarian = One who is between seventy and seventy-nine years old.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The art of growing fruits, flowers and vegetables
exp: 'The art of growing fruits, flowers and vegetables' is called 'horticulture' (Hindi: बागवानी, उद्यान-विज्ञान). Other options: neurology (तंत्रिका-विज्ञान); genealogy (वंशावली-विज्ञान); astrology (ज्योतिष).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MAESTRO
opts: One who lives a solitary life for religious reasons
A soldier who fights for any country for money
One who regards the whole world as his country
exp: MAESTRO (Hindi: संगीत-आचार्य) means: A distinguished conductor or musician. The other options are the meanings of mercenary, hermit, cosmopolitan respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Gregarious – Living in flocks or groups; fond of company
Olfactory – Relating to the sense of smell
exp: 'Impassable' means 'That cannot be crossed or travelled over' (अगम्य, दुर्गम), not 'Feeding on flesh' (that is 'carnivorous'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: GLUTTON
opts: One who makes an excessive display of learning
exp: GLUTTON (Hindi: पेटू) means: One who eats too much. The other options are the meanings of misanthrope, philatelist, pedant respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: APICULTURE
exp: APICULTURE (Hindi: मधुमक्खी-पालन) means: The rearing of bees. The other options are the meanings of seismology, viticulture, sericulture respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AUTOBIOGRAPHY
opts: A group of sheep or birds
The life story of a person written by himself
A long narrative poem about heroic deeds
The decision of a jury or court on a case
exp: AUTOBIOGRAPHY (Hindi: आत्मकथा) means: The life story of a person written by himself. The other options are the meanings of epic, verdict, flock respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: OMNIPRESENT
opts: One who is unable to pay his debts
exp: OMNIPRESENT (Hindi: सर्वव्यापी) means: One who is present everywhere. The other options are the meanings of insolvent, culpable, verbatim respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: NUMISMATICS
opts: The study or collection of coins
exp: NUMISMATICS (Hindi: मुद्राशास्त्र) means: The study or collection of coins. The other options are the meanings of ornithology, osteology, ichthyology respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: LEXICOGRAPHY
exp: LEXICOGRAPHY (Hindi: कोशरचना) means: The art of compiling dictionaries. The other options are the meanings of viticulture, pisciculture, seismology respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: DEMOCRACY
opts: Government of the people, by the people, for the people
Government by a king or queen
Absence of government and law in a country
exp: DEMOCRACY (Hindi: लोकतंत्र) means: Government of the people, by the people, for the people. The other options are the meanings of monarchy, bureaucracy, anarchy respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: BURROW
opts: A hole dug by a rabbit or a fox
A place for the treatment of invalids or convalescents
A place where weapons are kept
exp: BURROW (Hindi: बिल) means: A hole dug by a rabbit or a fox. The other options are the meanings of sanatorium, mausoleum, armoury respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: MISER
opts: One who is between eighty and eighty-nine years old
One who makes an excessive display of learning
One who hoards wealth and spends as little as possible
One who secretly listens to the private conversation of others
exp: MISER (Hindi: कंजूस) means: One who hoards wealth and spends as little as possible. The other options are the meanings of octogenarian, pedant, eavesdropper respectively.

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Insomnia; (B) Hereditary; (C) Synopsis; (D) Proprietor
List-II: (1) The owner of a business; (2) Inability to sleep; (3) Passed from parents to children; (4) A brief summary of a book or play
exp: Correct matching: Insomnia = Inability to sleep; Hereditary = Passed from parents to children; Synopsis = A brief summary of a book or play; Proprietor = The owner of a business. Hence A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: HORIZON
opts: A book containing the words of a language arranged alphabetically with meanings
The line at which the earth and sky appear to meet
A direct vote by the people on a single political question
exp: HORIZON (Hindi: क्षितिज) means: The line at which the earth and sky appear to meet. The other options are the meanings of dictionary, referendum, decade respectively.
